title: Scaling a One-Person Brand with Open-Source Automation
excerpt: Building an n8n automation engine to rival IGN and conquering Docker to build tools for creators.
preview: I’ve been thinking about building this tool for a while, pushing it off longer and longer. I’m finally kicking the procrastination monkey off my back and diving into n8n.

bodyHtml:
Kicking the Procrastination Monkey

I’ve been thinking about building this tool for a while, pushing it off longer and longer. I’m finally kicking the procrastination monkey off my back and diving into n8n.

If you’re asking yourself, “What is n8n?”, it’s an open-source automation workflow. Learn about n8n here. Think Zapier or Make (you’re probably still wondering what the hell that is), but with the power to basically automate anything if you have a little bit of technical know-how.

To keep things organized, I created an epic in GitHub. That’s how I organize all my work for content, web development work, and everything I’m doing lately. It’s a great tool, and I’ll talk about it in another post.

Working Smarter, Not Harder

My current objective is defined as building a complete automation tooling suite for all my social media workflows.

I’m just one person, so I need to work smarter, not harder. The biggest bottleneck I have right now is content distribution.

Right now, I’m building a workflow that triggers a social media blast the moment I publish a Substack article or YouTube video. It’ll automatically push the posts to all available platforms where I can connect for free. That means Threads, Bluesky, and Facebook pages. I’m skipping X because they charge for their API, which is stupid.

I’m strictly utilizing free tiers until this is fully monetized. I’m more than halfway there now, so if you want to support the page, please hit subscribe!

The Creator SaaS Vision

Once this is built out, I’ll package it into a SaaS (Software as a Service) tool for other creators, even if it just runs on a “buy me a coffee” model. I know a lot of creators who need this kind of tooling but don’t know how to set it up. I want to listen to creators and expand on it as I go.

The Technical Roadmap

My technical roadmap for this week involves:

  • Repurposing an old Windows machine into a Linux box to run everything locally and avoid cloud hosting fees. I’ve been delaying this because of massive imposter syndrome. I keep feeling like I won’t be able to do it, but I know I can.

  • Utilizing Docker for all of this. I’ve learned and relearned Docker so many times, going back to when I had to teach myself Docker and Kubernetes as a Junior Software Engineer at PlayStation.

Just to make things harder for myself, I might even incorporate Kubernetes into this project as well. Regardless, it’s time I fully master it.

  • I’ll admittedly be using Claude to help me build this out, but I have it set to learning/teaching mode, so I actually do the work myself. It’ll take longer, but it’ll be worth it to properly upskill.

I’m doing all of this while burning through a 3-hour NetworkChuck playlist on n8n and the Hermes AI agent, which is another tool I’ll be integrating into all this. NetworkChuck is a great YouTuber who makes “ethical hacking fun”, and I’m honestly just listening to him in the background while I work because he’s awesome.

Navigating the Ecosystem

This build is probably going to take about a week to get done, but it should be a lot of fun. I just thought I’d share an update on what I’m actually working on. I was supposed to be doing a 30-day challenge on YouTube, but failed that miserably. I’m going to get back to it, but I’d love to just keep writing and keep you all in the loop as I figure it all out.

This is just another post sharing my journey of trying to upskill myself, figuring out this creator ecosystem, and navigating this weird economy we’re living through.

Speaking of which, while doing all this social media stuff, I’m still trying to find a software engineering job.

So if you’re hiring, please reach out to me on LinkedIn and hire me!

If anything here brings you value, I hope you’ll subscribe and check out my YouTube channels. Let me know if you have any questions about anything, and I’d love to share. Let’s chat in the comments.

See you in the next one. Peace.

title: Leveling Up: How Community and AI Are Transforming My Workflow
excerpt: I don’t use AI to do the work for me. I use it to teach me how.
preview: Lately, I feel like my posts have been a little too “me, me, me.” Today, I want to change things up and actually provide some value to you.

I’ll start by talking about the Claude community. If you aren’t familiar, it’s an incredible global network of people who are passionate about Claude. I’m part of the Orange County chapter. It’s an amazing organization that hosts events worldwide where people come together to code, build skills, share knowledge, and support one another.

Attending these events has shown me exactly how differently people use Claude and AI in their day-to-day work. AI is just AI at the end of the day, right? But seeing the diverse ways people apply it has been eye-opening. I met folks who use it purely conversationally, which was so smart that I immediately started doing it myself. I’ve also met people who use it in really simplistic ways, and others who use it to organize their entire calendar and daily life. It’s ultimately a tool, and learning how others integrate it can inspire you to figure out what works best for you.
bodyHtml:
Lately, I feel like my posts have been a little too “me, me, me.” Today, I want to change things up and actually provide some value to you.

Finding My People in the Claude Community

I’ll start by talking about the Claude community. If you aren’t familiar, it’s an incredible global network of people who are passionate about Claude. I’m part of the Orange County chapter. It’s an amazing organization that hosts events worldwide where people come together to code, build skills, share knowledge, and support one another.

Attending these events has shown me exactly how differently people use Claude and AI in their day-to-day work. AI is just AI at the end of the day, right? But seeing the diverse ways people apply it has been eye-opening. I met folks who use it purely conversationally, which was so smart that I immediately started doing it myself. I’ve also met people who use it in really simplistic ways, and others who use it to organize their entire calendar and daily life. It’s ultimately a tool, and learning how others integrate it can inspire you to figure out what works best for you.

Closing the Gap Between Technical and Creative

This mindset shift completely changed my workflow and helped me overcome my own avoidance of using AI. Even as someone who transitioned from working as a QA tester to a Junior Software Engineer at PlayStation (my last job), I felt like I had a lot of knowledge gaps. I used to be terrified that I couldn’t build a website from scratch. Now, these AI tools act as the perfect gap fill for my entire life, covering both technical and creative areas.

I need to make one thing extremely clear: I do not use AI to create content.

I know a lot of creators hate using AI in the creative process, and I get it. Instead, I use AI to teach me how to create better content. I’m using it to teach me how to master bounce flash photography, learn how to properly expose and color grade S-Log3 in DaVinci Resolve, and how to be a better filmmaker overall, even with improving the framing of my shots. It helps me learn the exact things I’ve always struggled with. I feel like I’m finally mastering Photoshop, and I literally spent 12 hours in it the other day.

Expanding Horizons with Google Developer Groups

Next up is the Google Developer Group. It is similar to the Claude community but slightly more business-focused. Local chapters host awesome events like hackathons and learning sessions where they teach you how to leverage AI and dive into new tools.

Being part of this group even led to an opportunity for me to go to Google I/O. I didn’t end up going this time, but just having the chance was incredible. I definitely hope to make it next time. You can gain so many skills just by getting involved in these spaces.

Leveling Up with Certifications

Finally, I want to highlight an awesome certificate opportunity. Google has a lot of certification programs, and I’m sure other platforms have their own learning paths too, but I specifically want to highlight the Google Cloud “Get Certified” program. They offer several great tracks, including one called GAIL (Generative AI Leader) and the Associate Cloud Engineer program.

I actually just signed up for the Cloud Engineer track myself. Getting certified is a fantastic way to level up your skills and make yourself more valuable in the industry.

Thanks for reading. All links are provided below so you can check these out. I know there are plenty more programs out there, and I plan to start sharing them in future posts. Let’s keep learning together.

Resource Links:

  • Claude Community: https://luma.com/claudecommunity

  • Google Developer Group: https://gdg.community.dev

  • Google Cloud “Get Certified” program: https://developers.google.com/program/gear/getcertified

bodyHtml:
If you didn't know, I have a website! I have been building up my social media brand, BE Unconventional HQ, for a while now. It is a personal project, but I am really excited about it.

Recently, I started learning Astro. I will admit I have been vibe coding, but I have been learning a ton along the way! And Astro is a framework I enjoy using.

If you have seen some of my other posts, you know I have a few different things going on. Right now, my main focus is building tools for content creators. The influencer and creator space is huge, and I think there are a lot of ways I can help.

Currently, I am developing three apps:

  1. An analytics collection tool to optimize the workflow of pulling stats and displaying them in a professional media kit.

  2. A monitoring app for cameras. I am excited about this one, especially since it will help me develop even more skills, mainly C++.

  3. An AI agent service using n8n to optimize my workflow when posting across multiple social media platforms.

"Cool, I know how to do this, but what do I do with it?"

My goal recently has been to focus on targeted learning and optimizing my workflow so that when I build something, it actually has a purpose. I don't want to go down the tutorial rabbit hole. At the end of a tutorial, I always think to myself, "Cool, I know how to do this, but what do I do with it?"

Instead, I have been looking at the tools I already use and asking how they can be improved. Even if a tool already exists, I look for ways to make it better.

“I don’t know how, so I’m going to learn how to do it!“

Claude and Google Antigravity have completely shifted my mindset from "I don’t know how, so I can’t do this" to "I don’t know how, so I’m going to learn how to do it!" That feeling is empowering. I am now able to actually develop the tools I need and, in the process, learn new skills to make myself a stronger candidate in the job market.

The market is incredibly competitive right now, and it is difficult, especially with all the recent industry layoffs.

I like posting things like this to share my progress, but also to inspire others to utilize the tools available right now. You can use them to upskill, level up, and build something real so that you can potentially find work or do something entrepreneurial to succeed in your own endeavors.

I hope everybody is having a great day, and I wish you all the best of luck.

Time for me to get back to work!

Andrew B., photographer, filmmaker, building in public and figuring it out as I go. I break down what's working and what isn't.
Follow the journey on YouTube: HeyThisIsAndrew

title: It Took Me Six Hours to Edit One Video
excerpt: It’s 11:56 PM and I almost didn’t do this today.
preview: I spent most of my day editing for Be Unconventional HQ. I posted one long-form video and one short, did a lot of prep work, applied for jobs, and continuously checked my email. Basically, today was just all about productivity.

Throughout the day, I kept thinking to myself, “How am I going to find time to actually record and post Day 3 of this challenge?” It got to around 8:00 PM, and I nearly gave up. I was really ready to just call it a night.

Then I told myself, “No. At the bare minimum, we’re going to try.” I decided that if I was going to do this, I was also going to challenge myself to get faster with editing, because right now, it’s taking me way too long to edit a single video.
I’d be embarrassed to tell you how long it took me to edit the one video for Be Unconventional HQ.

Yes, I’m a slow editor right now. That’s something I need to improve, and honestly, I’m still embarrassed that I had to admit that. But that’s also part of why I’m doing this. I’m trying to get better.
bodyHtml:
I spent most of my day editing for Be Unconventional HQ. I posted one long-form video and one short, did a lot of prep work, applied for jobs, and continuously checked my email. Basically, today was just all about productivity.

Throughout the day, I kept thinking to myself, “How am I going to find time to actually record and post Day 3 of this challenge?” It got to around 8:00 PM, and I nearly gave up. I was really ready to just call it a night.

Then I told myself, “No. At the bare minimum, we’re going to try.” I decided that if I was going to do this, I was also going to challenge myself to get faster with editing, because right now, it’s taking me way too long to edit a single video.

I’d be embarrassed to tell you how long it took me to edit the one video for Be Unconventional HQ.

It took me about six hours.

Yes, I’m a slow editor right now. That’s something I need to improve, and honestly, I’m still embarrassed that I had to admit that. But that’s also part of why I’m doing this. I’m trying to get better.

Better than yesterday

Now I’m tired, and I’m thinking about tomorrow. I’m thinking about the fact that tomorrow I want to do better than I did today. Or, better said, tomorrow I want to do better than I did yesterday. That’s the mindset I’m going into it with.

Being better than you were yesterday, every day. That’s going to be one of the mottos of this challenge.

I’m mass applying for jobs. I’m working on a 30-day challenge. I’m working to build a brand called Be Unconventional HQ. I’m also trying to optimize my time so I can practice my photography and start getting work as a photographer.

There’s a lot going on right now. And honestly, I’m scared.

Things didn’t pan out the way I thought they would, and now I’m betting on myself. Sometimes it genuinely feels like I’m gambling with my life, and I don’t know what’s going to happen.

But I’m still here.

What you missed

Day 2 was about failed starts.

I was looking over my Substack, Medium, and YouTube channel, and I was embarrassed by what I saw. I had started and stopped so many times. Sometimes there was a month between posts, sometimes a week or two, and more often than not, an entire year between posts.

It got so bad that when I told a friend of mine, someone who’s always been incredibly supportive, that I was going to do this 30-day challenge, she even said, “Are you going to do it?”

When one of the most positive and supportive people you know starts losing faith in you, that’s when you know you’ve failed.

I’m embarrassed by that, too. I need to earn back the respect and trust of my friends so they know I’m serious about this, because I want to succeed. I want to turn this into something.

Day 3 was about 2,000 job applications.

Two thousand job applications. Six interviews. Zero offers.

That’s it. That’s the story.

I feel like it’s relatable, although I also feel like I’m experiencing the worst of it right now.

Tomorrow

I’ll try to get up early, get my workout done, and get to the point where I can actually do another video tomorrow. Hopefully, I’ll be faster and better, and I’ll continue improving.

That’s really the goal.

I’m not going to promise that I’m going to post on Substack and Medium every single day. I’m already doing a lot, and even though these posts should technically be pretty easy to put together, it still takes time to format everything, edit it, and make sure it’s something I’m actually proud of.

I’m going to try my best. That’s all I can promise.

I don’t want to say, “I hope to see you tomorrow,” because if I’m not here tomorrow, I’ll feel like I’m lying. So instead, I’ll say, “I will see you soon.”

If you want to see me daily, check out my YouTube videos or anything else I’m working on. I genuinely appreciate it.

Thanks for reading this.

Peace.

bodyHtml:
Right now, the biggest barrier that I’m overcoming is myself because, at the end of the day, no one cares. The only person who’s doubting themselves is me.

I can’t believe I just did this. I just color-graded a video from start to finish.

I’m not going to lie, AI tools helped me. Don’t hurt me (to the people who don’t like AI in the creative workflow). I didn’t allow it to do anything except guide me in my learning process.

Thanks for reading Andrew’s Substack! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.

I just went from someone who knows nothing about color grading to someone who knows nothing about color grading, but used AI to get there.

I don’t like the idea of using AI tools to actually create content, but I do think they can be utilized as a way for us to advance our learning and improve our skills. I just went from someone who knows nothing about color grading to someone who knows nothing about color grading, but used AI to get there. What that allowed me to do is actually learn and understand vectorscopes and waveforms, and even how to use primary color wheels, things that an hour ago I had no idea about.

So, I think it can be useful. But, let’s get to the point of why I’m even talking today.

The Thief of Joy

We’ve all heard that comparison is the thief of joy. And when you’re putting work out there, it’s easy to look at what people are doing and think, “Why does my work not look like that?”

That’s the whole reason I even decided to color-grade this video that I’m doing today (yesterday; this is late). It’s because I’m always looking at other people’s work and thinking about why mine doesn’t match up. And you know what? The reason is that I didn’t put the effort in to learn how to do it.

I may have taken a shortcut by using AI to guide me, but I’m still going to learn from here. Now I know that I am actually capable of doing it. I hope to improve these skills to the point where I finally have that creative look that I’ve always wanted. But today, I just overcame a hurdle, a hurdle that’s going to get me one step closer to actually pursuing my creative journey.

Putting My Flag Down

Today (yesterday) is the start of a 30-day challenge for me. I’m putting my flag down, or whatever phrase you want to use. The truth is, I’m scared. I don’t think I’m going to get past three days; that’s how bad I am in terms of doubting myself. But regardless of what I talk about, regardless of how bad the video is, I’m going to put something out there.

My goal is to share my journey of building up these brands that I want to make, see whichever one succeeds, and then go from there. I’ve got three accounts:

  • Hey, This Is Andrew: behind-the-scenes insight into how I’m creating, building apps, utilizing modern tools as part of my broader creative growth portfolio, and honestly showing the real struggles of a creator.

  • Be Unconventional HQ: This is where I share about the things that I’m passionate about: movies, TV, gaming, and events. I just dropped a review for Spider-Man: Brand New Day. I even built a website, which, funny enough, I had an AI tool analyze to ask if it was good. It said: Yeah, it’s actually better than I thought it was going to be, and it far exceeds where you are in your journey.

  • Capture Create Caffeinate: A portfolio to showcase my work while pursuing cocktail photography and videography, and I think I’m pretty damn good. The one thing holding me back, again, is me. But, if I were to name the thing I’m using as an excuse, it’s flash photography.

I just got done color grading. If I can do that, then I can do this too. I can actually do it. I can learn fast. I can ramp up. I can do this. Moving forward, my mindset is going to be “I can do this.” Regardless of how I get there, I’m going to figure it out. I will use the tools available to me to learn and grow as a creator.

Overcoming the Biggest Barrier

I hope you’ll follow me on this 30-day challenge. Maybe you can relate. Maybe you’re somebody who looks at other creators and feels intimidated, or feels like your work doesn’t look or sound like theirs.

I’m so proud of the video I just made today, but the one thing I’m mad at is the fact that there was a lot of background noise. I had to use software to clean up the audio, and even now, I listen to it, and I’m hating it a little bit. But I still posted it, and I’m proud of myself for at least doing that.

Anyway, this is just a little rant, but in addition to posting videos for this 30-day challenge, I plan on just speaking my thoughts out loud here.

One note for you: This video is not the first video in this 30-day challenge. I had three false starts, and the third one is when I finally decided this was the video I was going to post. This was the hardest video to post; it’s the video that I recorded where I actually had to color-grade it because I shot it in S-Log3.

I created barriers for myself so that I could overcome them. Right now, the biggest barrier that I’m overcoming is myself because, at the end of the day, no one cares about me. The only person who’s doubting themselves is me.

So, I’m going to do this, and I hope you’ll follow along on the journey. Check out the links to all my socials below and let me know what you think. There’s probably something you’re interested in if you read this far.

I hope to see you tomorrow. Peace.

Thanks for reading Andrew’s Substack! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
